title: Defining, Understanding, and Detecting Online Toxicity: Challenges and Machine Learning Approaches
measurement_description: The paper surveys existing literature on toxic content detection. In relation to religion, it reviews and categorizes studies that measure or detect religious hate speech, Islamophobia, anti-Muslim sentiment, and religious intolerance in online content.
findings: The paper finds that the body of research on toxic content detection includes work on religiously-motivated hate speech. Specific topics identified in the surveyed literature include Islamophobia, anti-Muslim sentiment, and attacks related to religious identity. The review notes that most research is focused on English-language content and a few major platforms, indicating a need for broader, cross-lingual and cross-platform studies which would also apply to the detection of religious hate speech.
